paragraphs.en: Find answers beginning with a chosen letter and belonging to the given categories. For B, you might write Brazil for country, Berlin for city and beaver for mammal. Accepted answers score points; an answer nobody else gave is worth more.
Two to eight players take part. Each round has one judge, while the others answer. The judge neither fills in a sheet nor scores that round, and the role moves to the next person each round.

At the start of each round, the game draws a letter and six categories. You have 90 seconds to answer. Tab moves to the next field and Shift+Tab back to the previous one; each field announces its category and the letter.
You may leave answers blank and return to them later. Everything remains editable until you submit.
When finished, Tab to Finish answering and press Enter. You cannot change a submitted sheet. Others see your answers only after everyone has finished.
Ctrl+T reads time left. At timeout, the answers currently in the fields are submitted, even if some are blank. If everyone submits early, judging begins immediately.
Later rounds draw new letters. A used letter does not return until the alphabet is exhausted.
The judge checks that each answer begins with the right letter and fits its category. Players can discuss doubtful answers.

As judge, move between answers with Tab, choose a judgement with the arrows and confirm with Enter. Identical answers in a category are grouped, so one decision applies to everyone who gave that answer.
Award points as follows:
- A correct answer given by only one player earns 2 points.
- A correct answer shared by several players earns 1 point each.
- An answer given by one player may be accepted as partly correct for 1 point.
- A wrong answer or blank field scores zero.
After confirming every judgement, select Finish review and press Enter. The round's points are added and the next person becomes judge.
The usual target is 50 points. Once someone reaches it, finish the current cycle of rounds so everyone has judged equally often. The highest total then wins.

Players tied for first continue in a tiebreak. Only they answer, with another player judging. If everyone is tied, the judge keeps rotating as before. Continue until one player leads after a complete cycle.
S reads scores and V reads round information. Use these outside answer-entry fields.
In the table settings, choose whether to answer in English or Polish. This also determines the alphabet used for drawing letters.
Choose one of three separate difficulty pools, or make your own:
- Easy is the default. Its 29 categories include country, fruit and tool.
- Medium has 29 categories, such as capital city, film and car brand.
- Hard has 28 categories, such as mythological deity, jewelry material and unit of measurement.
- Custom lets you choose from all 86 categories.
You can separately choose one to nine categories per round instead of six, but no more than your selected pool contains.

- Enable Separate letter for each category to give every category in a round a different letter: for example, a vehicle beginning with D and food beginning with F. Each answer field and review item includes its letter. Letters are drawn again for the next round.
The host can change these rules before play:
- Answer time may be shorter or longer than 90 seconds. Zero removes the timer, so everyone must submit before judging begins.

- A fixed host judge replaces the rotating judge. The host judges every round and does not compete for points. Reaching the target is then resolved after a single round, without waiting for a judge cycle.
- The target may be changed from 50. Rotating-judge games still finish the whole cycle.
- Tied leaders may share victory instead of playing a tiebreak.
Tab: move to the next answer or judgement field.
Shift+Tab: move to the previous field.
Arrows during judging: choose a judgement.
Enter: confirm a judgement or a finish button.
Ctrl+T: read answer time remaining.
T outside text fields: read the letter or category letters and the judge.
S outside text fields: read scores.
V outside text fields: read round information.
